claim: Measured on a 192x64 block, DDMA constant fill (0.07 us a byte) beat CPU PUSH fill (0.20); dithered fills cannot use it, a pattern-row copy is no faster than PUSH, and per-row jobs lose.
limit: The notes' figures came from CSpect. On a KS1 (core 3.03.00, nxsuite D13) a constant fill took 2.88 clocks of 28 MHz a byte (about 0.10 us) and a copy 5.92. JNext 1.3.0 has no DDMA.

evidence.text: CSpect 4.5.9, 192 x 64 block, us a byte: LDIR 0.76, zxnDMA 0.18-0.21, DDMA 2D copy 0.18, PUSH fill 0.20, DDMA constant fill 0.07; dither rules the constant fill out; pattern-row copy = PUSH's speed, per-row jobs lose; only the view copy gains.
evidence.quote: 0.18-0.21, DDMA 2D copy 0.18, PUSH fill 0.20, DDMA constant fill 0.07.

evidence.text: KS1 Issue 2, core 3.03.00 (nxsuite D13): blitter constant fill 2.88 clocks of 28 MHz a byte; the other blitter operations measured 5.92; 0 bytes wrong.
